newsitem.title: USA: Oregon unemployment drops to 5.0 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Oregon unemployment drops to 5.0 pct in May.

text.p: Oregon's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped six-tenths of a percentage point to 5.0 percent in May, according to a state report issued on Tuesday.
May's unemployment was down from the April rate of 5.6 percent and March's 5.8 percent figure, Oregon's Employment Department said.

"Many construction, manufacturing and service workers got a jump on their summer jobs, and consequently the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped substantially," said David Cooke, an economist with the Employment Department.
Seasonally adjusted total nonfarm payroll employment expanded by 2,800 jobs in May, as compared to April's revised growth of 8,800 jobs.
Job gains over the past 12 months have averaged 4,600 per month, for an annualized growth rate of 3.7 percent, the department said.

In May, seasonally adjusted job gains were largest in trade, manufacturing, and construction. Declines were posted in services, government, transportation, communications and utilities, the department said.
